mechanism_narrative: A sustained two-week recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, as observed in the last two weeks, signals a gradual return to office-based routines, which will positively impact weekday retail footfall and produce higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES showing a sustained upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The recent decline of PARKS mobility into negative territory indicates a shift away from outdoor recreational activities, which will divert discretionary time and spending away from retail and recreation, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0% change from baseline.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases or remains stable over the next 14 days, even after PARKS mobility drops below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent slight increase in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility indicates a renewed confidence in public transport and office returns, which will synergistically boost RETAIL_REC as more people commute and engage in out-of-home activities over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both show week-on-week increases for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing concurrent increases.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently high RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating continued time spent at home, will suppress out-of-home retail and recreation activities, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, especially if work-from-home policies remain prevalent.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases significantly over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated above 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A stabilization and slight improvement in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, indicating essential errands are being completed, suggests a baseline level of out-of-home activity that could free up time for discretionary retail, leading to a slight increase in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above -5% for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable or improving above -5%.

mechanism_narrative: The observed week-on-week decline in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last two weeks indicates a persistent negative trend in discretionary out-of-home activity, which is expected to continue and drive RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC reverses its trend and increases over the next 28 days, relative to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of declining PARKS mobility and persistently high RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests a general retreat from out-of-home activities, both discretionary and essential, which will collectively depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0% and RESIDENTIAL remains above 7% for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days while PARKS declines below 0% and RESIDENTIAL remains high above 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained uptick in TRANSIT mobility, potentially driven by easing public transport guidelines or increased confidence, will facilitate greater movement for retail and recreation, leading to a modest increase in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT shows a week-on-week increase for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT increases for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC continues to decline in the following week.
